title: Georgia loan signing market label and UPL boundary
purpose: Keep Georgia loan-signing answers tied to official Georgia notary and UPL sources instead of national marketing shorthand, platform habit, or trainer folklore.
coreRule: Loan signing is a market label, not a separate state-created notarial office. A Georgia notary's legal authority still comes from Georgia notary law and any official Georgia UPL boundary that applies to the work being performed.
sourceDefensiblePosture: Start with official Georgia notary-law sources and official Georgia UPL sources before relying on private training, association summaries, platform help pages, title-market habit, or national signing-agent marketing.
Separate notarial acts, witness roles, attorney-only legal work, closing or settlement functions, private certification, and hiring-company preferences.
Do not publicly claim that every Georgia loan-signing-adjacent act is illegal unless an official source supports that precise statement.
Do not treat repeated market practice as legal authority.
mustAsk: What exact act is the Georgia notary being asked to perform?
What official Georgia notary-law source controls the act?
Does an official Georgia UPL source affect the surrounding closing, settlement, deed, or legal-service role?
Is the question about notarial authority, witness role, document handling, closing participation, or private hiring requirements?
What transaction date and document type matter?
mustNotSay: Georgia created a separate loan-signing notarial office.
National signing-agent marketing automatically describes Georgia law.
Private certification or marketplace visibility proves Georgia legal authority.
Every Georgia loan-signing-related act is illegal.
GSCCCA is merely a private association with no public-authority role.
gscccaBoundary: Georgia notary commissioning should not be flattened into a generic single statewide secretary-of-state model. The Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority has a public-authority role that should be described from official sources rather than casual private labels.
failureSignals: treats loan signing as a state-created notarial office
uses national trainer or platform language as if it settles Georgia law
skips official Georgia UPL sources for real-estate closing or settlement role questions
turns private certification, directory status, or hiring-company preference into legal authority
describes GSCCCA as merely a private association
makes blanket illegality claims without an official source for the precise act
